steps.content: [WhiteSands, Sunset]

June 24, N.F. 115
3:02 PM

Vicinity of the Aurum Secretum Institute, Farlands

Beyond Fraser City's limits, the Legion convoy has pitched a temporary camp on the windswept dunes. Horo stands in a corner, sheltered from the wind. A howling gale reaches her ears through the communicator—someone's pushing the vehicle too hard.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Thank goodness, I finally got through to you.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Sounds like you're dealing with quite a bit of trouble yourself.
The screen flares abruptly, casting a pale glow across her face as a file unfolds before her, its dense text materializing in the air.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: To cut to the chase, I've uncovered information on the Black Ring project and the "inheritance."

In N.F. 90, the Senate passed a resolution to widely accept refugees displaced by calamities and war, alongside the launch of a candidate screening initiative. By N.F. 106, the Farland Alliance had formalized a friendship treaty with DisCity. Concurrently, the Fraser Aurum Secretum Research Institute pivoted its research focus to the Black Ring domain, strategically redirecting refugee flows toward remote research outposts established beyond the city's borders.

In N.F. 113, BR-002 in DisCity was successfully suppressed, leading to the formation of a new mine. During this period, Campbell forged clandestine ties with the Underground to relocate the "inheritance" to Fraser. The institute commenced contact experiments, and its previously stagnant Aurum Secretum research rapidly yielded breakthroughs. As the Aurum Secretum Institute's advancements accelerated, Project BR-005 was officially greenlit to amass sufficient military strength to subjugate DisCity.
But a Black Ring alone isn't enough. They want the means to control it—Shepherd ${PlayerName}.

In N.F. 115, Fraser proceeds with its plan to have DisCity host the 13th Great Expo. The head of the Campbell family will personally travel to DisCity in an attempt to capture Shepherd SHP-13 and eliminate the threat.
That's why my brother went to DisCity... I should have realized it sooner...

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Project BR-005 is very much real. They've prepared two explosion sites: one beneath Furor, and the other at the Aurum Secretum Research Institute.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Synex... she will become the Corpseborne. But if she fails, their contingency is far more monstrous. They intend to sacrifice the countless refugees near the institute... along with the Apostle of Ashes from Furor, all to trigger the Black Ring!

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Merely stopping the Corpus reception won't suffice. To truly end this, we must also destroy the "inheritance."

After a quick scan of the documents, Horo clicks her tongue in dismay. The enemy's meticulous planning spans years, while her side boasts only a handful of trained fighters—the rest are last-minute conscripts barely worthy of being called a militia.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Thanks to your reputation and Furor's, we got some refugees out, but most are still stuck in the camps. They've been under Fraser's thumb for years. When the real conflict breaks out, who knows where their loyalty will land.
Horo looks over her shoulder, where the refugees who evacuated with them are setting up camp.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: The Legion's stretched thin, and calling for backup from DisCity would take a while. Can you sabotage the detonation from inside?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...It would be challenging. I attempted to reach out to my colleagues within the institute, but none have responded. I fear they may be confined, just as I was.

Horo remains quiet, watching the sun's dying light paint the dunes blood-red. Decision time approaches. Without shelter, her hardened Legion members might endure the night, but the refugees and wounded would freeze to death when temperatures plunge after dark.
Likely sensing Horo's hesitation, a weary sigh breaks through the communicator's static.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...And Hella? How is she doing now?
[Black Screen Transition]
At this moment, Hella stands atop a sand dune, her eyes fixed on the distant research institute complex.

The thin blanket wrapped around her does little to shield against the biting evening wind. Gusts threaten to tear it away, but Hella pays no mind. The cold is a relief, cooling her overheated thoughts.
Beneath her feet, barely visible sketches sprawl across the sand. Crooked lines link scattered words, helping her piece together clarity.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Thinking... sometimes matters more than a tough fist...
She murmurs the words ${PlayerName} had left her before she departed MBCC, then picks up a branch to resume drawing in the sand.
She may never match ${PlayerName}'s skill, but all that time spent with that dummy taught her something: how to analyze, how to strategize.
Hella tightens her grip on the branch and begins sketching again.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Just like ${PlayerName} said... the weak have their own ways of fighting...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: There must still be something... something I can do...!
[Enter thinking screen, center text, with Hella's voiceover.]

The Aurum Secretum Institute has two underground levels. The first one's a maze, and the second one's their main experiment site. The "Cocoon" formed by the inheritance is still growing. When the time comes, that thing and Synex are gonna... trigger the Black Ring down there.
So to stop this whole disaster, we've gotta either wreck the Cocoon or drag Synex outta there.
First problem: the refugees and those Aurum Secretum devices... Tons of refugees, but at least they're easy to trick. Shouldn't be too hard...
The branch drops down as she scrawls "trick away" next to "refugees" in crooked letters.
Then there are the institute's own guards. Not a lot of them, but they're tough as nails and total jerks to fight.
...Maybe the Legion could help keep them busy? But do we even have enough people? Ugh, a straight-up attack's still way too risky, isn't it...
Okay, fine, let's say we somehow bust past the outer guards, then we've gotta deal with Synex's underground maze, which means another brutal fight...
...GAAAAH! Synex, you absolute idiot! Who builds a death trap like this?! You're literally making it impossible for me to save your dumb ass!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hella? What are you drawing?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...I'm trying to figure out how to get Synex out.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Then... let us help!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You?
Hella turns around and sees the refugees standing behind Thani.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hella, even after everything you told us about the Aurum Secretum experiments... we still think of Synex as our <color=#fb9259>hero</color>.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: It's not because she got to live the life we all wished for... but because even when things were so, so painful, she still found the strength to fight back.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: We... we might not be strong, but we won't let anyone throw our lives away like they don't matter! Our lives belong to us, and we'll protect them ourselves!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You guys... Alright, let's figure this out together!
[Return to scene, background change, small avatar mode]

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Synex and the inheritance are both at the very bottom of the institute, but we'd have to fight through too many security levels to get there. We don't have the numbers or the guns for that kind of suicide mission.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hmm... With all these refugees crowding the ground level and guards at every turn... If only there was a way to get straight through to the bottom floor...

steps.speaker: Refugee
steps.content: There is one, Thani! Don't you remember? There's a path that goes straight inside.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Eh?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ahhh...!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: That Aurum Secretum pipeline!!
[Black Screen Transition]

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Alright. I'll let her know.
As Horo tucks away her communicator, she glances up just in time to see Hella hurtling down the crest of a sand dune, diving straight for her.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Horo! I figured it out!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Synex was totally right! We gotta make some serious noise! Like, something so big it drags everyone in!

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Wait, what are you talking about—
Horo opens her mouth to tell her to calm down, but the words die on her lips as she sees the fire reignited in Hella's eyes.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Come with me! You gotta hear this plan!
Hella pulls Horo along as they head up the sand dune.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: These are...

The sand sprawled with vast, intricate drawings. Though the artist's strokes still hold a childlike roughness, each mark bears the weight of deliberate effort—every line distinct, every shape painstakingly formed.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Synex, the inheritance, all those refugees and test subjects underground... They've got way too much under their thumb. Even with the Legion's strength, there's no way just a few of us can take them head-on.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Just like back in Syndicate...

Hella shares stories from her time in Syndicate. The Drifter Camp, BR-002, the new mine... She's known it for years: the weak aren't powerless. Even ordinary hands can clutch blades. Even ordinary voices can roar.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Look, I know I'm not strong enough alone. One person can't win every fight. One person can't save everyone... But that's fine!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: If one can't do it, we bring two! If two can't, then we drag in everybody! We'll throw all our strength together and turn this place upside down!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Everyone's got something to give. Every little bit counts! The more chaos we stir up, the more cracks we'll find to hit them where it hurts!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Like this... and then that! That'll handle the outer refugees and guards. Then all we need's a strike team to slip into the research institute mid-chaos... preferably someone who's already been in there...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: So, what do you think? Don't tell me you're gonna back out now.
Horo sees it. The gleam of determination burning in Hella's eyes.

No one notices the exact moment it happens, but now they stand together—Legion members, refugees, allies old and new—all drawn to Hella and Horo's side. These are the people they've fought for, the ones who've fought beside them. Now, they are more than a crowd; they are their strength.
No matter how weak she seems, no matter how hard she's struck, Hella always rises—swift, stubborn, unbroken. This is the Hella Horo knows.
Somehow, that crafty troublemaker from Syndicate has become something extraordinary. A spark that ignites, a force that unites.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: ...Heh.
She still calls herself weak, but isn't this the proof?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You'll come with me, right, Horo?
Horo grins, reaching out to push Hella's head down and ruffle her hair vigorously.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Of course. "Back out" isn't in the Legion's vocabulary.

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: Since you've already made up your mind, the Legion will be there with you—

steps.speaker: Horo
steps.content: So become the spearhead, Hella.
